treatment.logline: Inside a rain-bound cash van, a personal recording unsettles Dinu before a business directive changes his route; his wrist thread holds the unanswered question of allegiance.

arc.beat: A working driver enclosed by the wet city; a faded photograph reveals another attachment.
arc.feeling: Isolation with a trace of intimacy.

arc.beat: A recorded absence becomes a private burden.
arc.feeling: Concern held behind a working face.

arc.beat: An incoming connection replaces concern with instruction.
A glance at the thread precedes a consequential turn.

treatment.approach: Keep every moving image inside the van. Tight, restrained handheld frames place wet, congested light behind one contained driver. Establish the photograph before playback and show each device source before its voice begins. The 90-second must bin includes deliberate same-event master and listener coverage, not 90 seconds of new business. The reference cut can hold pauses or select among overlapping coverage without multiplying the events.

treatment.geography: Dinu remains seated at the driver's position throughout. Shoot from the adjacent passenger side and passenger-side rear quarter, staying on one side of his forward driving axis. The photograph and phone rest on the dashboard; the phone is within his right-hand reach. Assign the red thread to his left wrist consistently. The industrial approach is registered through the windscreen, not an exterior cutaway.
treatment.key_image: Dinu's lowered eyes and the red thread on his steering wrist share the frame before his gaze returns to the road.
advice: Do not explain the thread or manufacture a response to either voice.
Treat the recording and live connection as different sound textures, both sourced from the phone.
Rain, engine, wipers and breathing carry the scene; no score.
The printed photograph is dressing, not a new live appearance.
Coverage repeats the same actions for editorial choice; it must not create repeated messages or repeated turns.

moments.cut_uses: Tight single includes eyes and steering wrist; passenger-side master carries the turn; forward-oblique master holds its completed direction. These are consecutive phases, not repeated manoeuvres.

editor_notes: The 88-second, 13-clip must bin is source material, not an 88-second assembly: the full-line master and reaction takes overlap. Play L3 and L5 once each, without trimming, and use the handles to select angles.
Use 2A-1 and 2B-1 for the working drive; 2C-1 establishes the printed photograph. Keep its figures static as a photograph, not live people.

Show 2D-1 and its playback indicator before L3; show 2D-2 and its incoming identification and acceptance before L5. The phone remains on the dashboard; Dinu's right hand returns to the wheel after each single press. Keep the thread on his left wrist.

For L3 match 2A-2, 2B-2 and 2E-1 on the same forward gaze, brief grip tightening and closed lips. For L5 match 2B-3 and 2A-3 on the same steady driving and jaw movement. The off-screen voices never appear as performers.

The final turn is divided into consecutive phases: 2F-1 holds the wrist glance and return to the road; 2A-4 shows the single steering change; 2G-1 sustains the new direction. Match hand and wheel positions at the joins and do not create a second turn or an arrival.

The supplied packet does not specify clothing or a phone mounting method: keep Dinu's attire identical throughout and place the phone resting within right-hand reach on the dashboard. The photograph stays beside it.
Build rain, wipers, engine, road wash and breathing in post where a silent source is requested. Keep the recording and live connection acoustically distinct; no music is needed.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options; these takes provide clean continuous sources. None is required by the reference cut. No slow motion, mirror work, fast finger work, physical contact or sharply resolved crowd is planned.

editor_notes: The 88-second, 13-clip must bin is source material, not an 88-second assembly: the full-line master and reaction takes overlap. Play L3 and L5 once each, without trimming, and use the handles to select angles.
Use 2A-1 and 2B-1 for the working drive; 2C-1 establishes the printed photograph. Keep its figures static as a photograph, not live people.

Show 2D-1 and its playback indicator before L3; show 2D-2 and its incoming identification and acceptance before L5. The phone remains on the dashboard; Dinu's right hand returns to the wheel after each single press. Keep the thread on his left wrist.

For L3 match 2A-2, 2B-2 and 2E-1 on the same forward gaze, brief grip tightening and closed lips. For L5 match 2B-3 and 2A-3 on the same steady driving and jaw movement. The off-screen voices never appear as performers.

The final turn is divided into consecutive phases: 2F-1 holds the wrist glance and return to the road; 2A-4 shows the single steering change; 2G-1 sustains the new direction. Match hand and wheel positions at the joins and do not create a second turn or an arrival.

The supplied packet does not specify clothing or a phone mounting method: keep Dinu's attire identical throughout and place the phone resting within right-hand reach on the dashboard. The photograph stays beside it.
Build rain, wipers, engine, road wash and breathing in post where a silent source is requested. Keep the recording and live connection acoustically distinct; no music is needed.

Speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in and split screen are post-only options; these takes provide clean continuous sources. None is required by the reference cut. No slow motion, mirror work, fast finger work, physical contact or sharply resolved crowd is planned.

review.why: The isolated left-wrist thread punctuates the glance, and the interior road view carries the completed choice into an unresolved ending.
A rear-quarter profile holds Dinu's roadward attention under L5 without duplicating the frontal listener coverage.
A focus shift between the active phone and the photograph's edge connects the recording to the shared past; the locked clips already supply held facial reactions.
The locked phone insert already establishes caller identification and acceptance; another device angle would repeat the same beat.
The locked phone insert already shows the recording source and its activation before the voice begins.
The locked photograph insert gives the required clear hold; the later dashboard focus shift adds a distinct association without repeating that introduction.
A rain-filtered interior establishing view gives the enclosed city an atmospheric opening without moving outside the van.
